tasks.title: Fix COMMISSIONING.md Stage 5a FILL-start log examples (BUG-001)
tasks.description: Stage 5a 'Record per fill' tells the operator to read recovery off a 'FILL start' line, but its example shows recmin=2 for recovery=8200ms and claims 'truncated: 599999 ms -> 0'. formatFillLogEvent() derives recmin = recovery_ms/60000 (truncated), so 8200ms -> recmin=0 and 599999ms -> 9 (as README.md:51 and COMMISSIONING.md:350/364/525 correctly show).

subtasks.title: Correct recmin=2 -> recmin=0 and '599999 ms -> 0' -> '-> 9' in Stage 5a; grep-verify all recmin examples
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: plan/001_53984f832581/bugfix/001_db6d94af3d0d/architecture/system_context.md sections 2-3: firmware/jug_filler/jug_filler.ino:1354-1357 prints 'FILL start backstop=%umin recovery=%lums recmin=%u' with recmin = (unsigned)(e.b / 60000u) (truncated). 8200/60000 = 0; 599999/60000 = 9. Exactly two defective values exist repo-wide; the examples at COMMISSIONING.md:329/350/364/525 and README.md:51 are already correct - do not touch them.
2. INPUT: docs/COMMISSIONING.md as shipped (Stage 5a 'Record per fill' spans lines 430-453). No code or schema dependency; this is a pure documentation edit.
3. LOGIC: Apply exactly two verbatim corrections from system_context.md section 3: line 434 '- from `FILL start backstop=44min recovery=8200ms recmin=2` - the' becomes the same line with recmin=0; line 436 'truncated: 599999 ms -> 0;' becomes 'truncated: 599999 ms -> 9;'. Then run the verification recipe (system_context.md section 6): grep -n 'recmin=' docs/COMMISSIONING.md README.md and assert every printed recmin equals floor(recovery_ms/60000) of its own example line and every prose truncation claim says 599999 ms -> 9. Implied TDD: the grep is the failing test before the edit and must pass after.
4. OUTPUT: corrected docs/COMMISSIONING.md Stage 5a, byte-identical elsewhere, consumed as-is by P1.M2.T3.S2 (changeset-level sweep) which re-runs the same grep as its acceptance check.
5. MOCKING: none - static documentation edit, no services, no build.
6. DOCS: Mode A - this subtask IS the doc fix (docs/COMMISSIONING.md Stage 5a); no separate docs task rides along.

tasks.title: Fix README serial-log table BTN example (BUG-002)
tasks.description: README.md:49 documents the BOOT-press log row with example 'BTN short 1234ms'. A hold >= BUTTON_LONG_PRESS_MS (1000 ms) classifies as long, and the logged hold is the raw edge-to-edge span, so a 1234 ms hold always logs 'BTN long 1234ms' - the printed short example can never occur and contradicts the PRD section 5.1 classification the same row describes.

subtasks.title: Replace 'BTN short 1234ms' with a <1000 ms value in the README serial-log table row
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: plan/001_53984f832581/bugfix/001_db6d94af3d0d/architecture/system_context.md sections 2 and 4: config.h:28 BUTTON_LONG_PRESS_MS = 1000; ButtonClassifier (jug_filler.ino:150) returns LongPress when holdMs >= 1000; the BTN line is emitted at jug_filler.ino:1685 with the raw edge-to-edge hold. Therefore every logged 'BTN short <n>ms' has n < 1000 and every 'BTN long <n>ms' has n >= 1000. spec/SPEC.md section 5.1 (lines 117-126) is the classification source of truth.
2. INPUT: README.md as shipped, 'Serial logging' table (lines 41-78); the BTN row is line 49. No code dependency.
3. LOGIC: In the line-49 row replace `BTN short 1234ms` with a value strictly < 1000 ms (suggested: `BTN short 340ms`); keep `BTN long 1500ms` (valid, 1500 >= 1000). Change nothing else in the row or table. Verify with system_context.md section 6 recipe: grep -n 'BTN short\|BTN long' README.md docs/COMMISSIONING.md and assert short examples < 1000 and long examples >= 1000 everywhere. Implied TDD: grep fails on 1234 before, passes after.
4. OUTPUT: corrected README.md serial-log table row, consumed by P1.M2.T3.S1 (changeset-level README sweep) which re-runs the same check.
5. MOCKING: none - static documentation edit.
6. DOCS: Mode A - this subtask IS the doc fix (README.md serial-log table).

subtasks.title: Session A dry bench check and Stage-2 power-rail measurement with evidence capture
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: bench_evidence_package.md section 1 (BINDING power safety: RP2040-Zero VSYS ties directly to USB VBUS with no diode - never USB and buck together; 12 V may feed the MOSFET module alone; dry-fire clicks < 5 s each; rail check is buck-only with USB unplugged so its evidence is multimeter readings, not serial) and section 2 Session A checklist (boot banner POWER_OR_RESET, LED off in IDLE, 1 Hz 'S1= S2=' streaming not pinned at 0/4095, BTN short/long on release, dry-fire x2-3 with ordered prefixes FILL start -> BASE ok -> VALVE open -> VALVE close -> ABORT, LED solid during FILLING).
2. INPUT: docs/bench/ templates from P1.M2.T1.S2; firmware already flashed from the repo (pico env builds clean; no reflash needed for this session).
3. LOGIC: With the rig: (a) buck-only rail check per Stage 2 - preset buck with board disconnected (4.9-5.1 V), then buck at board 5 V pin (4.9-5.1 V), recorded in the rails markdown sheet; (b) reconfigure USB-only (buck disconnected), run Session A per its template, capture the 115200 stream to the date-stamped session-A log with operator header, tick each prefix/LED checklist item, note valve clicks heard Y/N. If the rig is unavailable, mark the session BLOCKED with reason in the index - never fabricate log contents.
4. OUTPUT: docs/bench/<date>_session-A-dry-bench.log and <date>_rails.md evidence files plus index rows; proves the rig operational (banner, BTN, dry-fire) for P1.M2.T2.S2.

6. DOCS: Mode A - evidence artifacts under docs/bench/ with date-stamped filenames plus the index update; spec/SPEC.md remains the source of truth and is not edited.

subtasks.title: Sessions B and C: Flow 1 (abort + recomputed restart) and Flow 2 (successful fill) with evidence capture
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: bench_evidence_package.md section 2 Sessions B and C: Flow 1 fresh boot must show 'FILL start backstop=30min recovery=0ms recmin=0', mid-fill short press yields 'VALVE close' -> 'ABORT attemptms= openms=', and the restart line MUST NOT be recovery=0ms - it comes from the backstop table (44 min at small recovery per the shipped config), not FRESH_BOOT_BACKSTOP_MIN (SPEC 6.1/6.2). Flow 2 requires >= 60 s of valve-open before the first dip (early-trip guard), dip sensor 1 only ('VALVE close' -> 'TRIP sensor=1 fillms='), dip sensor 2 within the 12 s confirm window ('CONFIRM pass sensor=2 durms=' -> 'DONE attemptms= openms='), green LED triple-pulse (3x200 ms on/200 ms off, 1000 ms pause), then short press 'ACK done' and the next press starts a new fill. Hand-dip sensors in a cup; USB-powered session per the power rules.
2. INPUT: operational rig proven by P1.M2.T2.S1 (banner/BTN/dry-fire pass); session-B/C templates from P1.M2.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: Execute both sessions per their templates on USB-only power, hand-dipping sensors; capture each session's stream to its date-stamped log; tick the ordered-prefix checklists; explicitly verify the Flow-1 restart line shows recovery != 0ms and a table-derived budget, and that Flow 2 closes the cycle (post-ACK press starts a new fill). Record any mismatch as a discrepancy entry rather than editing evidence.
4. OUTPUT: docs/bench/<date>_session-B-flow1-abort.log and <date>_session-C-flow2-success.log plus index rows; consumed by P1.M2.T2.S3 (fault paths reuse the wet-sensor technique) and P1.M2.T2.S5 (consolidation).
5. MOCKING: none possible - physical task; sensors hand-dipped, valve dry-fired (no water through the valve; keep opens < 5 s where the flow requires aborting).
6. DOCS: Mode A - evidence artifacts plus index update.

subtasks.title: Session D fault paths: baseline fault, no-confirm fault, optional guard faults, with blink-code verification
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: bench_evidence_package.md section 2 Session D (SPEC 7/4): fault LED = red blink groups of N (250 ms on/250 ms off, 2000 ms pause), latching until RESET. Baseline fault: start with a wet sensor tip -> 'VALVE close' -> 'FAULT baseline sensor=N code=N count=' with the CRITICAL assertion that NO 'VALVE open' line precedes the fault (the plausibility gate refuses to open). No-confirm fault: trip sensor 1 after >= 60 s open, never dip sensor 2 -> after the 12 s window 'FAULT confirm sensor=2 code=2 durms=' with 2-blink groups. Optional guards: 'FAULT earlywet/earlytrip sensor=N code=N fillms='. Backstop expiry ('FAULT backstop code=3 budget= openms=ms') only if time permits - a recorded skip with reason is acceptable.
2. INPUT: rig operational with flows verified by P1.M2.T2.S2; session-D template from P1.M2.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: Execute the fault-path session on USB-only power: wet-sensor start (verify gate + blink code + latch, RESET clears to a fresh boot banner), then the no-confirm path, then optional guards as time permits; capture the stream; check off each expected prefix, blink cadence, and the no-valve-open assertion. RESET between latched faults as the template directs. Any observed-vs-expected mismatch goes to the discrepancy entries.
4. OUTPUT: docs/bench/<date>_session-D-fault-paths.log plus index row and any discrepancy entries; consumed by P1.M2.T2.S5.
5. MOCKING: none possible - physical task; faults induced by hand-dipping sensors (wet start) and withholding the second dip.
6. DOCS: Mode A - evidence artifacts plus index update.

subtasks.title: Session E optional watchdog-reset check via temporary never-committed hang patch (or recorded skip)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: bench_evidence_package.md sections 2-E and 5 (scout-verified): config.h contains zero #define/#if (constexpr only) and no UNIT_TEST-adjacent symbol exists anywhere in firmware/, test/, or platformio.ini - so the deliberate hang must be ADDED temporarily, e.g. a local '#if BENCH_HANG_TEST ... while(true){} ... #endif' placed inside loop() AFTER the watchdog feed point, flashed, run, then REVERTED; never committed. Watchdog: WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_S = 8, fed every loop pass; success evidence is the boot banner 'JugFiller boot (reset cause: WATCHDOG)' (jug_filler.ino:85-87, 1657) plus valve-closed/LED-off/no-auto-restart after reset.
2. INPUT: rig operational with all prior sessions green (P1.M2.T2.S1-S3); session-E template from P1.M2.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: USB-only power: apply the temporary hang patch locally, build+flash, start a fill, observe the ~8 s reset with the WATCHDOG banner and valve-closed behavior, capture the stream to the date-stamped session-E log, then REVERT the patch and confirm 'git status' shows no firmware diff; the evidence file records that the patch was reverted. This check is OPTIONAL per the original contract - a documented skip (with reason, e.g. policy against temporary firmware patches) recorded in the index is an acceptable outcome; never fabricate the capture.
4. OUTPUT: docs/bench/<date>_session-E-watchdog.log or a recorded skip entry, plus a clean firmware tree (patch reverted) - verified before P1.M2.T2.S5 consolidates.
5. MOCKING: none possible - physical task; the temporary patch is the isolation mechanism itself (it exists only on the bench flash, never in the committed tree).
6. DOCS: Mode A - evidence artifact plus index update; the temporary define is documented in the evidence file, not in config.h (config.h stays untouched).
